alleg:中山:-9999.n: The Xianyu of the White Di; not enfeoffed by Zhou

alleg:义渠:-9999.n: A Western Rong state; not enfeoffed by Zhou

alleg:六:-9999.n: Of the Yan surname, descendants of Gao Yao; no record of enfeoffment by Zhou

alleg:吴:-585.n: Shoumeng claims the title of king

alleg:吴:-9999.n: Descendants of Taibo, enfeoffed by Zhou

alleg:巢:-9999.n: A small Huai Yi state; no record of enfeoffment by Zhou

alleg:庸:-9999.n: No record of enfeoffment by Zhou

alleg:徐:-9999.n: The rulers of Xu style themselves king (bronze inscriptions name "King Yichu of Xu" and "King Geng of Xu"); the Chunqiu, following Zhou usage, calls the ruler "the viscount of Xu"

alleg:楚:-606.n: King Zhuang of Chu parades his army on the outskirts of the Zhou capital and asks about the size and weight of the tripods

alleg:楚:-671.n: King Cheng of Chu sends tribute to the Son of Heaven, who bestows sacrificial meat on him

alleg:楚:-704.n: Xiong Tong proclaims himself King Wu

alleg:楚:-9999.n: Xiong Yi was enfeoffed with land befitting a viscount or baron

alleg:舒:-9999.n: A small Huai Yi state of the Yan surname, now submitting to Chu, now rebelling against it; no record of enfeoffment by Zhou

alleg:莱:-9999.n: A Dongyi state that never joined the Zhou covenants

alleg:蜀:-9999.n: Not enfeoffed by Zhou; the rulers of Shu style themselves king

alleg:越:-9999.n: Not enfeoffed by Zhou; its rulers later style themselves king

fall:-478.p: King Hui of Chu kills Duke Min of Chen and destroys Chen.

fall:-487.p: Duke Jing of Song destroys Cao and seizes Yang, earl of Cao.

fall:-495.p: Chu destroys Hu and seizes Bao, viscount of Hu.

fall:-505.p: King Zhao of Chu, after recovering his state, destroys Tang.

fall:-506.p: Cai destroys Shen and kills Jia, viscount of Shen.

fall:-512.p: Wu destroys Xu and Zhongwu, and Zhangyu, viscount of Xu, flees to Chu.

fall:-520.p: Xun Wu of Jin destroys Gu of the White Di.

fall:-525.p: Xun Wu of Jin destroys Luhun, and the viscount of Luhun flees to Chu.

fall:-530.p: Jin destroys Fei of the White Di.

fall:-531.p: King Ling of Chu lures Marquis Ling of Cai to his death and destroys Cai, making it a county; Cai is restored in 529 BC.

fall:-534.p: King Ling of Chu destroys Chen and makes it a county; King Ping restores it in 529 BC.

fall:-548.p: Chu destroys Shujiu, and all of the Qunshu pass to Chu (Shuliao in 601 BC and Shuyong in 574 BC had already fallen).

fall:-567.p: Duke Ling of Qi destroys Lai and moves Lai to Ni; the same year Ju destroys Zeng.

fall:-594.p: Xun Linfu of Jin destroys the Lu lineage; the next year Jin destroys the Jia lineage and Liuxu, and in 588 BC Qianggaoru, and the Red Di are wiped out.

fall:-611.p: King Zhuang of Chu joins with Qin and Ba to destroy Yong.

fall:-623.p: King Mu of Chu destroys Jiang.

fall:-627.p: The Qin army fails in its surprise attack on Zheng, destroys Hua and turns back; the land of Hua later passes to Jin.

fall:-635.p: Duke Wen of Wey destroys Xing.

fall:-640.p: Duke Mu of Qin destroys Rui.

fall:-641.p: Duke Mu of Qin destroys Liang.

fall:-648.p: Huang relies on Qi and does not serve Chu, and Chu destroys Huang.

fall:-655.p: Duke Xian of Jin borrows a road through Yu, besieges Shangyang and destroys Guo, then on the way back surprises and destroys Yu.

fall:-661.p: Duke Xian of Jin destroys Huo, Wei and Geng, granting Geng to Zhao Su and Wei to Bi Wan.

fall:-678.p: King Wen of Chu destroys Deng (the same year Duke Wu of Quwo destroys Yi, and Jin is united under the Quwo line).

fall:-680.p: King Wen of Chu destroys Xi and takes Xi Gui.

fall:-681.p: When the people of Sui stay away from the Assembly at Beixing, Qi destroys Sui.

fall:-684.p: Duke Huan of Qi destroys Tan, and the viscount of Tan flees to Ju.

fall:-688.p: King Wen of Chu destroys Shen and makes it a county (one view: 687 BC).

fall:-690.p: Duke Xiang of Qi attacks Ji, and the marquis of Ji "leaves his state for good".

fall:-767.p: Duke Wu of Zheng destroys East Guo and makes the land of Kuai into Xinzheng.

fall:-769.p: Duke Wu of Zheng destroys Kuai.
